_json_ready hand-rolls a recursive copy of a list-or-dict value, while the other half of this same change copies the same shape with copy.deepcopy at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:190 and :192, and queue_admission.py already uses copy.deepcopy at eleven further sites (:542, :724, :1664, :1773, :1843, :5179, :5206, :5455, :5512) for exactly this purpose. Two copy mechanisms for one capability inside one change, and _json_ready is the narrower one: a tuple or any other container leaf is returned shared rather than copied, so the docstring's guarantee holds only for the two shapes it names. copy.deepcopy would have satisfied it whole.

the third case's assertions (rebuilt.images == [], rebuilt.inputs == [], rebuilt.compares_with == "", rebuilt.admission_findings == []) pass whether the rebuild takes the dataclass default or drops a stored value entirely, because a dropped value lands on the same default; what this case actually guards is that the rebuild does not raise when stored lacks the key, and the first case's field-by-field loop at line 81 guards the presence direction. Harmless as written, but the case should not be read as covering 'a stored value survives' for those four fields.
